picks.name: HermesEnabler
picks.desc: Enable Hermès Watch Faces on any Apple Watch devices
picks.readme:
# HermesEnabler 2

[English](README.md) · [Tiếng Việt](README.vi.md) · [한국어](README.ko.md) · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [繁體中文](README.zh-TW.md) · [日本語](README.ja.md) · [Español](README.es.md) · [Français](README.fr.md) · [Deutsch](README.de.md) · [Português](README.pt.md)

![](image.png)

> Supported on watchOS 27.0 through 27.3 beta 1.
> If you’re using an unsupported watchOS version, use [Clocky](https://github.com/pookjw/Clocky).

## Installation

### macOS

On macOS you can install the prebuilt IPA with Sideloadly or build the app directly with Xcode. Either way, the iPhone must be paired with the target Apple Watch, and the Watch must run a supported watchOS version.

#### Install the IPA

1. Download the IPA from [Releases](https://github.com/pookjw/HermesEnabler/releases).
2. Install [Sideloadly](https://sideloadly.io) on your Mac, connect your iPhone with a cable, and select it in Sideloadly.
3. Drag the IPA into Sideloadly and enter your Apple ID. Turn off **Use automatic bundle ID**, set a fixed Bundle Identifier, and start signing.
4. On the iPhone, open **Settings → General → VPN & Device Management** and trust your developer certificate.
5. On the iPhone, open **Settings → Privacy & Security → Developer Mode**, turn it on, restart, and confirm.
6. On the iPhone, open the **Watch** app, go to **My Watch → Apps**, and install **HermesEnabler2** on the Watch.
7. On the Apple Watch, open **Settings → Privacy & Security → Developer Mode**, turn it on, restart, and confirm. If the option is not shown, install the Watch app first and check again.
8. Open **HermesEnabler2** on your Apple Watch and follow the steps in the app.

#### Build with Xcode

1. Open [HermesEnabler2.xcodeproj](HermesEnabler2.xcodeproj) in Xcode.
2. Select your Apple Watch as the run destination and click **Run**.
3. Open **HermesEnabler2** on your Apple Watch and follow the steps in the app.

### Windows

Windows uses [WatchBridge](https://github.com/AdminZachary/iloader-for-windows), a community tool that prepares Developer Mode and installs an IPA containing both an iPhone host app and a Watch app. It is not affiliated with Apple or with this project.

1. Install **Apple Mobile Device Service** by installing [iTunes](https://www.apple.com/itunes/) or the **Apple Devices** app from the Microsoft Store. WatchBridge needs it for USB and Wi-Fi communication. WebView2 is built into Windows 11.
2. Make sure your iPhone is paired with the target Apple Watch. WatchBridge supports only one paired Watch at a time; if more than one is paired, the preparation step stops instead of guessing.
3. Download `watchbridge-windows.zip` from [WatchBridge Releases](https://github.com/AdminZachary/iloader-for-windows/releases/latest), extract it, and run `WatchBridge.exe`. The executable is unsigned, so Windows SmartScreen may warn on first launch.
4. Download the IPA from [Releases](https://github.com/pookjw/HermesEnabler/releases). Use the original IPA that contains both the iPhone host and the `Watch/*.app`; Watch-only packages are not supported.
5. Connect the paired iPhone over USB and select it in WatchBridge.
6. Pair the Watch and confirm the trust prompt on the Watch. Request the **Developer Mode** switch, then on the Watch open **Settings → Privacy & Security → Developer Mode**, turn it on, restart, and confirm. Return to WatchBridge and click **Check again**. WatchBridge does not enable Developer Mode or restart the Watch for you.
7. Sign in with your Apple ID, select the HermesEnabler2 IPA, and start signing and installation. WatchBridge installs the iPhone host app first, then the Watch app.
8. Open **HermesEnabler2** on your Apple Watch and follow the steps in the app.

> Developer-mode preparation requires a USB connection. After pairing over USB once, installs and renewals can use Wi-Fi.

## Cautions

- watchOS 26 is not supported.
- In Sideloadly, disable **Use automatic bundle ID** and use a fixed Bundle Identifier. Keep the same Bundle Identifier and A

picks.readme:
# App Store Compliance Playbook Catch App Store and Google Play rejection causes before the reviewer does. A reference and a pre-submission guard for iOS and Android apps that is plain about what a scan can prove and what still needs a person. It does not guarantee approval. Read it as a website at [mjmirza.github.io/app-store-compliance](https://mjmirza.github.io/app-store-compliance/). [![Apple App Store](https://img.shields.io/badge/Apple_App_Store-000000?logo=apple&logoColor=white)](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/) [![Google Play](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google_Play-414141?logo=googleplay&logoColor=white)](https://play.google/developer-content-policy/) [![Claude Code](https://img.shields.io/badge/Claude_Code-ready-000000?logo=anthropic&logoColor=white)](#how-you-actually-use-this) [![OpenRoots ORA 2.3](https://openroots.org/badge/ora.svg)](https://openroots.org/licenses/ora/2.3) [![CI](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/mjmirza/app-store-compliance/ci.yml?branch=main&label=CI)](https://github.com/mjmirza/app-store-compliance/actions) [![PRs welcome](https://img.shields.io/badge/PRs-welcome-2ea44f)](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/mjmirza/app-store-compliance?style=social)](https://github.com/mjmirza/app-store-compliance/stargazers) [![Forks](https://img.shields.io/github/forks/mjmirza/app-store-compliance?style=social)](https://github.com/mjmirza/app-store-compliance/fork) [![Follow mjmirza](https://img.shields.io/github/followers/mjmirza?label=Follow&style=social)](https://github.com/mjmirza) **If this saves you even one rejection, leave a star, fork it, and follow along. That is the whole ask.** [Star this repo](https://github.com/mjmirza/app-store-compliance)  |  [Fork it](https://github.com/mjmirza/app-store-compliance/fork)  |  [Follow on GitHub](https://github.com/mjmirza)  |  [Follow on X](https://twitter.com/MirzaJhanzaib)  |  [next8n.com](https://next8n.com)
## Start here Pick one row. The time shown is for that first step. | You are | Do this first | Time | |---|---|---| | About to submit, and you can open a terminal | Run the two commands below | 2 minutes | | Already rejected | Open [the appeal playbook](docs/MISTAKE-PATTERNS.md#the-appeal-playbook) | 10 minutes | | Not a developer | Open [the checklist](docs/PRE-SUBMISSION-CHECKLIST.md) and do its first two checks | 5 minutes | | Using an AI coding tool (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Grok, Qwen, Kimi and more), and want this on every submit | Go to [the install](#install-it-into-your-ai-coding-tool) | 1 minute | The two commands. Needs git and bash. The first downloads this playbook. The second scans your app. Nothing is installed and nothing in your app is changed. ``` git clone https://github.com/mjmirza/app-store-compliance ~/repositories/app-store-compliance bash ~/repositories/app-store-compliance/agent-os/hooks/app-store-compliance-guard.sh "/path/to/your/app" ``` Replace only `/path/to/your/app`, with the folder that holds your Xcode project or your Android app. Keep the quotes, they keep a folder name with a space in it whole. To get the path without typing it, drag the folder from Finder or your file manager into the terminal window. A small project scans in about a second, a large one can take up to a minute, and the guard prints the time it took. Findings print first, critical ones on top, each with the file and line that triggered it when there is one. The last lines tell you where you stand. | Verdict line starts with | It means | Do next | |---|---|---| | `BLOCKED.` | A critical rejection risk was found | Fix each `[CRITICAL]` line using the `fix.` line under it, then run the same command again | | `CLEAR.` | No critical ri

# Modern Web Guidance (Source) This repo is the source repository for [GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance) and includes the code and documentation for authoring, calibrating, and evaluating its contents. [**Modern Web Guidance**](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/modern-web-guidance) is a set of skills that embed web platform expertise, best practices, and browser compatibility data directly into your coding agents. It helps to steer your coding agents away from legacy patterns, and instead toward solutions that harness the power and capabilities of the modern web platform. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) and [GOVERNANCE.md](./GOVERNANCE.md) for how we work on the project and orientation of the codebase. --- *Stewarded by the Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, and MDN teams, alongside the web development community.* [Documentation](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/modern-web-guidance) · [Eval Dashboard](https://googlechrome.github.io/modern-web-guidance-src/) · [Source Code](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src) · [Report an Issue](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src/issues) ## Quickstart ```shell npx modern-web-guidance@latest install ``` This command runs an interactive wizard to install Modern Web Guidance. See [Alternative Installation Methods](#-alternative-installation-methods) below. Requires Node.js 22 or later. #### Try it out (without installing) ```shell # Search for relevant guides npx modern-web-guidance@latest search "animate a dialog modal backdrop" # Retrieve a guide by ID npx modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "animate-to-from-top-layer" # Scan a codebase for legacy patterns to modernize npx modern-web-guidance@latest legacy-scan . ``` ## Why? Coding agents often default to older patterns because LLM training data contains vast amounts of legacy code. This often leads them to generate bloated JavaScript for tasks that now have native, high-performance web platform solutions. Even if a model knows an API exists, it often lacks the density of real-world, modern implementation patterns required for production-ready code. **Modern Web Guidance bridges this gap.** Our skill's CLI returns targeted, expert-curated guidelines directly into your agent's context window, focusing on: * **Modern Browser APIs**: Helping models correctly structure APIs they frequently misuse. * **Performance & Accessibility**: Preferring platform-level APIs that can be optimized by the browser and include built-in accessibility affordances. * **Responsible Fallbacks**: Guiding models to use sensible, lightweight fallbacks instead of heavy polyfills or legacy libraries. ## What's Included? We cover the past several years of the web platform's new features, all the way up to the cutting edge. The guides are **designed to be token-efficient**; we run evals enabling us to prune lowest-common-denominator content that models already know. ### Core Disciplines

🎨 User Experience

Smooth visual states (View Transitions, entry/exit animations, parallax scroll, CSS scrollbar-col

picks.name: dsh-superagent-prototype
picks.desc: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System
picks.readme:
# dsh-superagent

> **Research prototype for reference only, not an official DeepSeek product.** This code grew out of our team's day-to-day development work, with much of the engineering done by coding agents. Treat it as research code, not production-ready software. It may still contain bugs, and its coding style and engineering practices may be inconsistent. Review and adapt it before using it in your own environment.
>
> We have adapted it for publication, so it is not identical to our internal version or the implementation described in *Exploring Super-agent Design: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System*. Some designs discussed in the article are directions for future development and are not implemented in this prototype.

dsh-superagent is a proactive coding agent for one GitHub repository, packaged as a bundle for [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.deepseek.com/en/harness/). It listens to GitHub and, optionally, Feishu. When someone allowed asks the agent for work, it opens a work item, works on it in its own agent session and directory, and answers in the original conversation, for example with a pull request. A web panel shows what needs a person.

It is also a way of working with an agent: **take as little human attention as possible, and give as much value as possible.** An agent that can act for a whole team can also waste a whole team's attention, so it acts only when asked or when a rule the team wrote allows it, and speaks only when someone must act or can use a result. [docs/000-philosophy.md](docs/000-philosophy.md) explains the principle and what it asks of the operator.

## Setup

Setup has many steps, so an agent does it with you. Ask your coding agent:

> Read SETUP.md in this repository and set up dsh-superagent with me.

It asks one short question at a time, shows the full plan once, and then installs and configures everything. [SETUP.md](SETUP.md) is what it follows.

## Documentation

Read the numbered documents in order; each builds only on the ones before it.

- [000 Philosophy](docs/000-philosophy.md)
- [001 Domain model](docs/001-domain.md)
- [002 Authorization](docs/002-authorization.md)
- [003 Execution](docs/003-execution.md)
- [004 Prompts](docs/004-prompts.md)
- [005 Panel](docs/005-panel.md)
- [006 Deployment](docs/006-deployment.md): manual setup, configuration, upgrades and troubleshooting
- [007 Architecture](docs/007-architecture.md)
- [008 Cookbook](docs/008-cookbook.md): adding a Source

## Development

`pnpm check` runs the typecheck, the tests and the build.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

picks.readme:
Agent Skills for use with Obsidian.

These skills follow the [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification), so they work with any agent that supports skills, including Claude Code, Claude, ChatGPT, Antigravity, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Grok Bot, Hermes Agent, Kiro, Muse, OpenCode, and [many more](https://agentskills.io/clients).

## Installation

Obsidian is an official plugin for Claude, ChatGPT, Dots, Cursor, Grok Bot, Hermes, and Kiro. Most other agents can install the skills from GitHub.

### Claude

Add [Obsidian](https://claude.ai/customize/plugins/id/a38fa062-ebd3-48e0-9a0a-1875a6e94ad5%40anthropic-plugin-directory) from the official Claude plugin directory.

For the Claude Code CLI use:

```sh
claude plugin marketplace add obsidianmd/obsidian-skills
claude plugin install obsidian@obsidian-skills
```

From within a Claude Code session:

```sh
/plugin marketplace add obsidianmd/obsidian-skills
/plugin install obsidian@obsidian-skills
```

To get new skills later, run `claude plugin update obsidian@obsidian-skills`.

### ChatGPT

Add [Obsidian](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugins_6aee4fde227881919d61b034b1c31096) from the ChatGPT plugin directory. The plugin works in ChatGPT, Codex, and Dots.

To install from this repo instead:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace add obsidianmd/obsidian-skills
```

Then install Obsidian from the plugin directory in Codex or the ChatGPT desktop app.

### Antigravity

In the Antigravity CLI, run:

```sh
agy plugin install https://github.com/obsidianmd/obsidian-skills
```

### Grok Bot

Open [Obsidian for Grok Bot](https://x.ai/bot/plugin/88871845) and select **Add to Grok Bot**.

### Muse

Ask Muse to install the skills from https://github.com/obsidianmd/obsidian-skills.

Muse runs in Meta's cloud, so the `obsidian-cli` skill doesn't work there. If you use Obsidian Headless in Muse, you sign in and sync your vault in Meta's cloud.

### Cursor

Install [Obsidian](https://cursor.com/marketplace/obsidian) from the Cursor Marketplace.

### Hermes Agent

Install [Obsidian](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/marketplace/obsidian) from the Hermes Marketplace, or run:

```sh
hermes plugins install obsidian
```

### Kiro

```sh
kiro-cli powers install obsidian
```

### GitHub Copilot, OpenCode, and other agents

Install with [npx skills](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills), which asks which agents to install into:

```sh
npx skills add https://github.com/obsidianmd/obsidian-skills
```

To install by hand, copy the folders in `plugins/obsidian/skills/` into your agent's skills folder, e.g. `~/.copilot/skills/` for GitHub Copilot.

## Release maintenance

Update the plugin version in every manifest with:

```sh
./scripts/bump.sh patch
```

The script also accepts `major`, `minor`, or an explicit version like `1.1.0`.

Gemini CLI installs from the latest GitHub release, so publish a release for each version, tagged with the version number. The `Gemini release archive` workflow then attaches `obsidian-gemini.tar.gz`, which has real copies of the skills. Don't attach other files to a release, because Gemini CLI only picks a file when there's exactly one; otherwise it falls back to the source archive, which has no Gemini manifest. To build the archive locally, run `./scripts/package-gemini.sh`.

| [obsidian-markdown](plugins/obsidian/skills/obsidian-markdown) | Create and edit [Obsidian Flavored Markdown](https://help.obsidian.md/obsidian-flavored-markdown) (`.md`) with

picks.readme:
# unslop

Created by Damir Sokolovsky ([@heydamir](https://x.com/heydamir)), who started the [Unslopping series](https://x.com/heydamir/status/2115063463063998736) on X.

![A vibecoded dashboard unslopping itself, frame by frame](skills/unslop/references/refs/story-dashboard-frames.webp)

unslop is a skill for Claude Code, Codex and Google Antigravity that turns vibecoded, AI-looking UI into a designed interface with its own character. It finds the slop first, the purple gradients, glows, emoji labels, shouty copy and uneven spacing, then sets a direction from your product and fixes the screen pass by pass like a designer doing a redline review. It works in whatever your screen is built with, like Next.js, React, Vue, Svelte, Tailwind or plain HTML and CSS, on dashboards, apps and landing pages, and even on a live site when all you have is a link.

## Install

For Claude Code, install it as a plugin. Run this in a terminal to get it in every project:

```bash
claude plugin install unslop --marketplace heydamir/unslop
```

On an older Claude Code without `--marketplace`, the same in two steps:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add heydamir/unslop
claude plugin install unslop@heydamir
```

To get it in a single project only, run the install from that project's root folder, the one you start Claude Code in, and add `--scope local`. To turn it on for everyone who works in the project, add `--scope project` instead and commit `.claude/settings.json`. Each teammate then runs this once in their own copy of the project:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add heydamir/unslop
claude plugin install unslop@heydamir --scope project
```

Then start a new Claude Code session, or run `/reload-plugins` in one that is already open.

To update, run `claude plugin update unslop@heydamir`, or turn on auto-update for the heydamir marketplace under Marketplaces in `/plugin`.

If you copied unslop into `~/.claude/skills/` or a project's `.claude/skills/` before, delete that copy, or `/unslop` keeps running it instead of the plugin.

For Codex, ask it to install the skill straight from this repo.

```
$skill-installer install https://github.com/heydamir/unslop/tree/main/skills/unslop
```

Or copy it by hand into `~/.agents/skills/`, or into `.agents/skills/` inside a single project.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/heydamir/unslop
mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills && cp -r unslop/skills/unslop ~/.agents/skills/
```

For Google Antigravity, copy the skill into your skills folder.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/heydamir/unslop
mkdir -p ~/.gemini/config/skills && cp -r unslop/skills/unslop ~/.gemini/config/skills/
```

For a single project, copy it into `.agents/skills/` inside that project instead.

To snapshot a live site or create a story video, install Playwright and its Chromium browser from the project directory where you run the skill:

```bash
npm install -D playwright
npx playwright install chromium
```

Story videos also require ffmpeg installed and available on your PATH.

## Use

In Claude Code, type `/unslop` with what you want, or `/unslop:unslop` if another skill already has that name. In Codex, type `$unslop` the same way. Or just ask in your own words and the agent picks the skill up by itself.

```
/unslop this dashboard
/unslop the hero of https://example.com
/unslop my landing page and make the story video so I can post it
```

It audits the screen and proposes a direction before it edits anything, so you can steer it early. If the screen is already good, it tells you so and suggests a few small refinements instead of redesigning it.

## What it does

- **Audit.** Lists every sign of slop with where it lives.
- **Direction.** Character, world, the one or two moments that carry the color, and a signature detail, all taken from your product.
- **Passes.** Spacing, color, icons, copy, type, layout, details, visuals and motion, in that order.
- **Visuals.** Shows your product instead of a glossy blob. When a hero needs a scene or an
